inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10-year government bond ~1.8% + equity beta ~1.0 x 6.7% ERP (mature-market ~5.5% plus ~1.2% China country premium) = ~8.5%. Ungeared (net cash, no long-term debt) so WACC = cost of equity. Same rate in every scenario: channel-disruption and margin risk are priced in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the rate.

inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with the non-US adaptations (routing row: operating company, non-US consumer). Want Want is an ungeared Mainland-China FMCG manufacturer (dairy/beverages 51%, rice crackers 24%, snack foods 24%); none of the bank/REIT/holdco/LIC conditions apply. First valuation of this ticker - no prior model in memory. Statements in RMB, HKEX quote in HKD (see fx_note). SBC-zero: band_position null. Net cash = cash and bank balances 11,383.4 + long-term bank deposits 4,476.0 - borrowings 2,656.7 = RMB13,202.7m at 31 Mar 2026 (lease liabilities excluded under treatment B). FY0 component check: EBITDA 5,577.6 - lease 141.3 - D&A ex ROU 694.7 = EBIT 4,741.6; x(1-25.5%) = 3,532 NOPAT; +694.7 - capex 1,010.5 = ~3,216 owner FCF vs reported FCF less finance income 3,473 (difference = the lease payment, which reported FCF leaves in financing, and interest paid on now-repaid debt). Cash-tax 25.5%: PRC statutory 25% plus withholding on repatriated dividends, against FY2026 cash tax paid RMB1,246m on ~RMB4.9bn PBT. Working capital is roughly nil (inventory + receivables + prepayments 5,199 vs payables + accruals + contract liabilities 5,320, distributors largely pay cash on delivery), so capture is a small -5% of the revenue change. Cash pile caveat: the Board cut the payout ratio to retain cash 'for potential uncertainties' and overseas capex; the bridge carries the cash at face, so the valuation assumes it is ultimately worth face to minorities - the largest single judgement in the number.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (6.0% 5yr, 10.7% 3yr) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (2.1%) and EPS (-0.8% 5yr). Book growth is an artefact of the payout cut (dividends RMB5.1bn FY2023 -> RMB1.7bn FY2026) retaining cash, not of business growth; revenue CAGR selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - PP&E/intangible capex) less finance income: FY2021 4,629 -> FY2023 3,516 -> FY2026 3,473 (RMB m). SBC is nil so the SBC adjustment does not move the series; the interest strip narrows the decline slightly because finance income fell from RMB469m to RMB43m as borrowings were repaid and deposits moved to long-term. Owner FCF has shrunk while revenue grew ~2%/yr: margin compression and capex doubling (FY2026 RMB1,010m vs RMB300-640m history) are the cause.

base.narrative: Revenue tracks its 2% five-year CAGR, decaying to 1%: emerging channels and snack foods offset high-single-digit declines in legacy wholesale/modern trade. EBITDA margin dips to 22.0% in FY2027 (H1 FY2026 operating margin was down 3pp; milk powder and palm oil cost inflation plus restructuring spend) and recovers only to 23.5%, below the FY2022-25 average, as discount snack chains keep pricing pressure on. Capex steps down from FY2026's Kaohsiung-plant peak to ~D&A.

bull.narrative: Emerging channels (snack-retail chains, e-commerce, instant retail, OEM) and overseas (Japan, India, Africa, Vietnam export base) scale fast enough to take group growth to 4-4.5%; new products keep a mid-teens revenue share. Milk powder and palm oil costs mean-revert, so gross margin rebuilds toward 47-48% and EBITDA margin returns to ~26%, between FY2024 and FY2025 levels.

bear.narrative: Legacy channels (70-80% of revenue) keep shrinking faster than emerging channels grow; the 'Conquering Cities' restructuring the Chairman says has missed targets for two years keeps failing; discount snack chains and private label force price and promotion concessions on Hot-Kid Milk and rice crackers. Revenue drifts down ~1%/yr for five years and EBITDA margin settles at 19% as marketing and staff costs stay elevated against a weak consumer.

scenario_narratives.base: Mature, ex-growth Chinese FMCG brand house: ~2% revenue growth decaying to 1%, margin compression stops at ~22% EBITDA and partially recovers to 23.5% (below the FY2022-25 average) as input costs stabilise but channel-transition spending persists.
scenario_narratives.bull: Channel transition succeeds and commodities ease: emerging channels plus overseas lift growth to 4-4.5%, gross margin rebuilds and EBITDA margin returns to ~26%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural share loss: legacy wholesale shrinks faster than snack-retail and e-commerce grow, revenue falls ~1%/yr for five years and EBITDA margin settles at 19% under promotional pressure from discount chains and private label.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% (from the 15% default) because margins have compressed in two consecutive reporting periods, management itself says the channel restructuring has underperformed for two years, and the Board cut the payout citing 'challenges facing future performance'. Base 55% because the balance sheet removes any solvency tail and the brand base is durable. Bull cut to 20% because it needs two independent things - commodity relief and a successful channel transition - to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cheap but decelerating. At the current price the market capitalisation is roughly twice RMB13.2bn of net cash, so the operating business is priced at roughly 4.5-5x owner FCF. The DCF says even a no-growth, lower-margin path is worth more than that; the gap is the market's discount for (i) structural channel decline and (ii) a controlling family that has chosen to retain rather than distribute the cash pile. The model carries the cash at face - the bear case is a flows case, not a cash-haircut case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash pile valued at face: if the controlling shareholder keeps retaining cash (payout cut to ~30%) and reinvests it at low returns, minority holders will not realise RMB13.2bn; a 50% haircut removes ~RMB0.56/share (~HK$0.66).
Structural channel disruption: legacy wholesale/modern trade (70-80% of revenue) declining high-single-digit as discount snack chains and e-commerce take share.
Unhedged input costs (whole milk powder, palm oil, sugar) drove gross margin -1.3pp in FY2026 and -1.1pp in H1 FY2026.
Repatriation: most cash and profit is in PRC subsidiaries; dividends upstream bear withholding tax (5-10%), only partly captured in the 25.5% cash-tax rate.
CNY/HKD: the HKD value moves one-for-one with the RMB; CNY has appreciated ~6% against HKD over the past year, which flatters the HKD conversion.
